title: EgoCaptioner: Towards Comprehensive and Fine-Grained Egocentric Video Captioning
excerpt: Egocentric video captioning requires fine-grained detail and accurate timing, yet current multimodal large language models (MLLMs) often miss brief actions, confuse their order, or misinterpret the wearer's motion. Existing caption formats also offer limited support for combining detailed narration with precise timing. We present EgoCaptioner, which pairs a video-level overview of the setting, participants, and the wearer's overall activity with timed steps whose narration adapts to varying perceptual demands and marks key moments at specific timestamps. We develop a coarse-to-fine annotation pipeline that establishes event structure before expanding step descriptions, yielding 50,000…

ai.summary: EgoCaptioner introduces a multimodal model that generates egocentric video captions combining a high‑level overview with timed step‑by‑step narrations to capture brief actions and motion order.
ai.why: It provides developers a template for building video‑understanding systems that need fine‑grained, temporally aligned descriptions.

title: AltRA-Test: An Alternative Annotator Test for LLM Judges Without Shared Annotators
excerpt: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used as judges and graders to replace human annotators, raising the question of when such replacement is statistically justified. To support such decisions, the Alternative Annotator Test (Alt-Test) was introduced for dense settings where all items are annotated by the same annotators. However, in many large-scale annotation settings, items are annotated by different subsets of annotators. We therefore propose the Alternative Annotator Test with Resampled Annotations (AltRA-Test), a statistical test that does not require that all items are annotated by the same annotators. AltRA-Test uses a bootstrap that resamples items, draws k human…

ai.summary: The paper proposes the Alternative Annotator Test with Resampling (AltRA-Test) to statistically justify replacing human annotators with LLM judges in large-scale settings where items are annotated by different subsets of annotators.
ai.why: Provides a statistical framework for developers to validate the reliability of LLM-based evaluation pipelines in distributed annotation scenarios.

title: RL Post-Training in Diffusion Transformers Is Activation Steering
excerpt: Reinforcement learning (RL) post-training substantially improves the visual quality, text rendering, and compositional accuracy of diffusion transformers. Because capabilities such as rendering requested text or composing multiple objects are inherently prompt-dependent, a natural hypothesis is that improving them requires learning complex, input-dependent transformations. To isolate how much of these gains an input-independent shift explains, we probe each RL-tuned model with a deliberately simple parameterization: a fixed set of steering vectors added to the block outputs of the frozen base model. ai.summary: A paper argues that improvements in diffusion transformers from RL post-training are largely due to input-independent activation shifts rather than complex, prompt-dependent transformations. The authors probe RL-tuned models to isolate the contribution of these shifts to visual quality and text rendering.
ai.why: Provides a technical insight into how RL fine-tuning works in diffusion models, which could guide more efficient training strategies for image generation.

title: TuringSpace: Grounding Spatial Intelligence in Action with Interactive CAPTCHAs
excerpt: Humans act in the visual world by inferring the 3D layout behind a 2D view, predicting how an action changes it, and correcting themselves after seeing the result. Can multimodal large language models (MLLMs) do the same? CAPTCHAs offer a natural test, since humans solve them through this very loop, clicking and dragging on the screen and adjusting after each result. Yet existing CAPTCHA benchmarks are largely solved and rarely spatial, while spatial benchmarks rarely require action. We therefore present TuringSpace, a synthetic web environment of 125 interactive CAPTCHAs that span five spatial abilities and must be solved through clicks and drags on the screen. ai.summary: TuringSpace proposes interactive CAPTCHA challenges that require spatial reasoning and action, testing multimodal LLMs on 3D layout inference and manipulation.

title: Depth Pro 2: Sharp and Temporally Consistent Metric Monocular Depth
excerpt: We present Depth Pro 2, an approach to estimating dense metric depth for images and video at full resolution. By analyzing prior methods for monocular depth estimation, we find that they commonly trade off temporal consistency and boundary sharpness: multi-frame methods favor consistency, single-frame methods favor sharpness. To overcome this trade-off, we train a single, scalable network that processes both images and video and predicts depth maps at native resolution. Depth Pro 2 produces depth maps that are metrically accurate, sharp, and temporally consistent all at once, outperforming prior work in all of these dimensions. title: Mind2Act World: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Embodied Mind, Physical Action, and Mind-Action Composition in Robotic Manipulation
excerpt: Embodied intelligence aims to let robots perform complex physical tasks with human-like adaptability and reliability, which requires three complementary capabilities: history-based cognitive reasoning, precise and timely physical execution, and the composition of reasoning and execution through environmental feedback. Yet existing benchmarks either evaluate reasoning and execution within the same tasks or assess them separately without their composition, so they reveal little about whether a failure comes from reasoning, execution, or their composition. title: WAM-Policy: World Action Models with On-Policy Distillation for Quadrupedal Loco-Manipulation
excerpt: Arm-free quadrupeds can perform loco-manipulation, walking on three legs while manipulating with a front leg, yet no existing policy for it follows language instructions. World action models (WAMs) have emerged as effective language-conditioned manipulation policies, but are pretrained for robot arms and sample slowly. The first, Cross-Morphology Policy Adaptation and Acceleration, adapts the arm-centric WAM to quadrupeds and distills the transferred policy into a student with one video and two action steps by on-policy self-distillation (OPSD). excerpt: Video understanding, particularly with accompanying audio, remains a central challenge in multimodal intelligence. Centering on joint audio-visual perception and reasoning, WeMM-Video unifies text, image, audio, and video processing within a hybrid-thinking paradigm, seamlessly supporting both a non-thinking instruct mode for fast, direct responses and a thinking mode for explicit step-by-step reasoning. title: ZeroVLN: Learning to Navigate without Supervised Fine-Tuning of the VLM Brain
excerpt: Representative vision-language navigation (VLN) methods typically couple a vision-language model (VLM) brain with a learnable action head and fine-tune the VLM brain on navigation-domain data to predict geometric goals. We introduce ZeroVLN, a slow-fast navigation framework that achieves effective navigation with zero navigation-domain SFT of the VLM brain. title: Posterior Matching Distillation
excerpt: Diffusion distillation accelerates image and video generation by compressing a pretrained teacher's iterative sampling process into a few network evaluations. Distribution-based methods achieve this by matching the student's output distribution to the teacher's. This matching is often driven by reverse-KL objectives, whose mode-seeking bias favors dominant teacher modes at the expense of diversity across samples. We introduce Posterior Matching Distillation (PMD), a new member of the distribution-based distillation family that combines mode-covering posterior sampling with any-step generation. ai.summary: Posterior Matching Distillation (PMD) is a new diffusion distillation method that matches the student’s posterior to the teacher’s, reducing mode‑seeking bias and preserving sample diversity.

title: Coda-DaVinci: Reimagining Video Generation with Code2Video
excerpt: Code2Video uses agent-authored 3D proxies to guide video generation, enabling explicit control over structure and dynamics.
